overall: The AG found the purpose for the 2010 discipline-related executive sessions concluded, ordered release of the minutes and listed documents, found the minutes' failure to list documents a violation, and cautioned the committee.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee had not released minutes of its 2010 executive sessions (May 28, June 29, July 19, Aug 30) after the discipline matter ended.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, in accordance with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f), the executive session minutes are required to be disclosed, subject to any applicable exemptions under the Public Records Law, G.L. c. 4, § 7, cl. 26.

allegations.summary: Complainant sought release of documents used by the committee during the 2010 executive sessions, not just the minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, consistent with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, we order that the following documents

allegations.summary: Minutes of the July 12, July 19, Aug 30 and Sept 8, 2010 executive sessions did not list documents used at the meeting, as the law requires.
allegations.key_passage: The failure to include a list of the documents used by the Committee during these executive sessions is a violation of the Open.Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee entered the May 28, 2010 executive session by roll call without stating a lawful purpose; the AG raised this on its own review.
allegations.key_passage: On May 28th, the Committee convened in executive session, but failed to state an appropriate purpose for entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Whether the June 29, July 19, Aug 30 and Sept 8, 2010 executive sessions were properly convened for discipline of an employee.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes also indicate that the deliberations that occurred during each of these executive sessions appropriately dealt with the discipline of an employee.

remedy: Release the executive session minutes of the May 28, June 29, July 19, August 30 and September 8, 2010 meetings, subject to the Public Records Law, within ten days of receipt of the determination.

Release the documents used at the May 10, August 30 and September 8, 2010 meetings (the Jefferson writing, the impoundment letter, the main motion, and draft public statements), subject to G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
Going forward, be cognizant of Open Meeting Law requirements, particularly listing all documents used during a meeting in the minutes.
remedy_passage: The Committee shall make the minutes available in a timely manner and no later than ten (1 0) days from the receipt of this determination.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
